dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: nirādhāraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā vikalpān na vikalpayet | tadātmaparamātmatve bhairavo mṛgalocane ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: Making the mind supportless, let one not construct thought-constructs; then, O doe-eyed one, in the self becoming the supreme self, there is Bhairava.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: 'all supports' means external supports, such as perceiving objects, and internal ones, such as imagination, concepts, pleasure and pain; one should be rid of thought-constructs (vikalpa). The constructing mind is the empirical self; the non-constructing awareness is the spiritual Self, witness of all states. Singh classes it as śāmbhavopāya. Wallis: 'don't fabricate'.
dharana.technique_name: A Supportless Mind That Builds No Thoughts
dharana.instruction: Let the mind rest on nothing, and do not build on any thought that appears.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 84' = verse 108 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 108 = 'Don’t fabricate (Y83 ~ C3)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 108 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 108 'Dharana 85', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 84. Not followed.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 108 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a mind leaning on nothing, outer or inner, and not building anything new.
geometry.svg_hint: an open space with no structure in it, a few faint lines dissolving at its edge
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Lean on nothing
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the mind lets go of every prop, outer and inner, and stops assembling thoughts. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The mind leaning on no support, outer or inner
attention.secondary: Not assembling thoughts; letting any that come pass

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Making the mind supportless, let one not construct thought-constructs; then, O doe-eyed one, in the self becoming the supreme self, there is Bhairava.
adiyogi.method_summary: Let the mind rest on nothing: no object, no image, no idea. When a thought appears, do not build on it; let it pass. Rest in the open awareness that remains.

honesty.disclosure: Door 084 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 84 (verse 108) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 084 is dharana 84, verse 108. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If this becomes effortful, rest attention lightly on the breath for a while. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
